title: You Are Right Too
text:
Nasreddin Hodja was once serving as the village judge. Two neighbors came before him with a quarrel that had been dragging on for weeks, and a small crowd gathered to watch.

The first man told his side of the story at length, with feeling and many details. Nasreddin listened carefully, nodded and said, "You are right."

Then the second man spoke. He told the same events in a completely different way, just as earnestly, explaining why his neighbor was to blame. Nasreddin listened carefully again, nodded and said, "You are right."

Nasreddin's wife had been listening from the next room. She came in, astonished. "Husband, what kind of judgment is this?" she said. "They cannot both be right!"

Nasreddin thought about this for a moment. Then he nodded to her as well. "You know, wife," he said, "you are right too."
lesson: Almost every account sounds convincing when you hear it alone. Before you take sides in a conflict, hear everyone involved, and stay humble about what you know.
people: Nasreddin Hodja as judge, two litigants, his wife
source: Nasreddin Hodja tales (Turkish and wider Middle Eastern folk tradition)
caveat: Nasreddin is a folk figure, and this joke is also told of other characters and rabbis.
